findings.title: RULE.CIT.DOI's check field says "weakness" but a hard-tier scan already enforces it
locations: src/Scans/doi_crosscheck.jl:61-67 — the `require_doi` loop flagging "a reference without a DOI or Open Library link on its title"
findings.description: RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK defines `weakness` as "a check is possible and none is built." For RULE.CIT.DOI ("Every reference carries a clickable DOI... identical in every copy") a check IS built: SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK's own header comment names RULE.CIT.DOI as one of the two rules it enforces, and its `require_doi` block (live in this package, tier hard, config flag true) is exactly that enforcement. RULES.toml nonetheless records RULE.CIT.DOI as an unpaid-check weakness — the rulebook misreporting its own coverage, the one thing RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK exists to keep honest. Failure scenario: a reader (or `gbgdev rules`/doctor tooling) trusts RULES.toml's `check` column to know what still needs a scan; taking RULE.CIT.DOI at its word, they either build a redundant second check or treat the rule as unenforced and stop trusting SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK's DOI-presence hits as authoritative.
findings.resolution_hint: Change RULE.CIT.DOI's `check` in policy/RULES.toml to `["scan:SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK"]` (matching RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE's row, since one scan enforces both rules).

findings.title: RULE.DOC.SHAPE's "`# Arguments` precedes any column-0 admonition" clause names a heading form no other rule in this package's rubric ever produces
locations: policy/docs-rubric.md:219 — "`# Arguments` precedes any column-0 admonition, and `# Fields` is last."
policy/docs-rubric.md:47-48 (RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM) — "uses the bulleted form led by `The arguments are:`" (a prose lead-in, never a heading)
findings.description: docs-rubric.md's only rule governing how a docstring's arguments are documented, RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM, mandates the prose lead-in `The arguments are:` and never a `# Arguments` Markdown heading; this package's own docstrings confirm it (0 uses of a `# Arguments` heading vs 30 uses of `The arguments are:`). Yet RULE.DOC.SHAPE's ordering clause, and the scan enforcing it, test specifically for a `# Arguments` heading — a structural element no other rule in this file ever sanctions the corpus to produce. (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md shows this heading is a different fleet consumer's (IT's) argument-doc style, so the clause is a deliberate cross-consumer accommodation, but that provenance is not disclosed anywhere in the rendered docs-rubric.md itself.) Failure scenario: a reader of docs-rubric.md in isolation — exactly how it is meant to be read, rendered whole into every consumer's session — hits this clause with no antecedent, and either concludes the rulebook is self-contradictory (ARGS_FORM bans the heading it implies) or hunts for a heading form that, for this package, never legitimately exists.
findings.resolution_hint: Either drop the `# Arguments`-heading half of RULE.DOC.SHAPE's ordering clause for a rubric whose ARGS_FORM never produces that heading, or add one clause naming `# Arguments` as the heading-form equivalent some consumers use instead of the prose lead-in, so the two rules read as one coordinated policy.
